import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 837

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/837](https://www.erdosproblems.com/837)
-/

namespace Erdos837

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Let $k\geq 2$ and $A_k\subseteq [0,1]$ be the set of $\alpha$ such that there exists some
$\beta(\alpha)>\alpha$ with the property that, if $G_1,G_2,\ldots$ is a sequence of $k$-uniform
hypergraphs with
$$\liminf \frac{e(G_n)}{\binom{\lvert G_n\rvert}{k}} >\alpha$$
then there exist subgraphs $H_n\subseteq G_n$ such that $\lvert H_n\rvert \to \infty$ and
$$\liminf \frac{e(H_n)}{\binom{\lvert H_n\rvert}{k}} >\beta,$$
and further that this property does not necessarily hold if $>\alpha$ is replaced by $\geq \alpha$.
What is $A_3$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_837 :
    {α : ℝ | α ∈ Set.Icc 0 1 ∧ ∃ β : ℝ, α < β ∧
    Hypergraph.HasDensityJump 3 α β true ∧ ¬ Hypergraph.HasDensityJump 3 α β false}
      = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end Erdos837

reformulations.difference: The shared HasDensityJump predicate selects induced subgraphs on vertex sets Sₙ, whereas the subgraph-density formulation in the literature permits arbitrary subgraphs Hₙ ⊆ Gₙ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An arbitrary subgraph on Sₙ has no more edges than the induced subgraph Gₙ[Sₙ]. Replacing it by that induced subgraph preserves the vertex counts and increases each normalized density. Both density sequences are bounded in [0,1], so monotonicity of real-valued liminf applies and preserves the strict lower bound. Conversely, every induced subgraph is a subgraph. This proves equivalence for each r, α, β and both Boolean settings, hence also for the negated condition and the set in the theorem. The full predicate equivalence was proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: Johnston, T. and Lu, L., Strong Jumps and Lagrangians of Non-Uniform Hypergraphs (2014), definitions of jumps, strong jumps, and weak jumps; sequence characterizations in Section 3. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1403.1220
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — bibliography used to locate primary literature.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-17.pdf — density-jump discussion on pp. 157–158 and associated references.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-35.pdf — discussion of growing hypergraph sequences and subgraph densities.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-24.pdf — discussion of possible densities of families of uniform hypergraphs.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1971-09.pdf — foundational density-increase problem for uniform hypergraphs.
https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1975-34.pdf — Erdős–Lovász hypergraph paper, examined for the original problem.

review.notes: No confirmed mathematical defect was found, but this is not an unconditional source-faithfulness certification; see the unresolved source check. Lean experiments verified uniform edge-count bounds, induced-density bounds, small and empty cases, eventual positivity of binomial denominators, and the answer's Set ℝ type. All density liminfs are bounded, avoiding default-value issues. The endpoint α = 1 belongs to the formalized set; Johnston–Lu explicitly includes this degenerate weak jump, so its strict-condition vacuity is not itself a defect.
